content.text:
I've built the Kestrel Coffee Roasters dashboard as a single `index.html` with all HTML, CSS and JavaScript inline. It uses only the figures you gave. I opened it in headless Chrome at 1440px and at 390px and both lay out correctly, with no sideways scrolling on mobile. A scripted run of the interactive parts passed and showed no JavaScript errors.

**What's on the page**
- **Navigation:** a dark sidebar on desktop with the company name and all seven items, with Overview marked as the current page. Below 1024px it becomes a slide-out menu opened from a menu button. It can be closed with the close button, by tapping outside it, or with Escape.
- **Top bar:** "Sales & Operations", "October 2026 · vs September 2026", the search field, and Mara Kim with the initials MK. On mobile the search field moves to its own row.
- **KPI cards:** each shows the change against September. The refund rate's −0.3 points is shown in green with an "improved" label.
- **Morning brief:** four short notes taken straight from your data: online revenue at a 12-month high, Riverside up 9.6%, Station Square the only café down, and two coffees to reorder.
- **Monthly revenue chart:** stacked columns for Online and Cafés with an All / Online / Cafés toggle. Exact values appear on hover, on tap, or with the arrow keys. There's also a "View data as a table" option.
- **Revenue by category:** horizontal bars rather than a pie chart, because six slices are hard to read.
- **Café table:** every column header sorts, and clicking again reverses the order. It starts sorted by revenue, highest first, and Riverside is tagged "Opened June 2026". On mobile this table scrolls sideways inside its card.
- **Top online products:** ranked by revenue.
- **Recent orders:** each status has its own colour, icon and label: Shipped (truck), Paid (check), Pending (clock, dashed outline) and Refunded (return arrow). On mobile each order becomes a stacked card.
- **Green coffee inventory:** sorted with the most urgent first, with a marker at 7 days. Brazil Cerrado and Ethiopia Guji are flagged "Reorder", using a red striped bar plus an icon and a label.

**Design choices**
I used the design skill's "data-dense dashboard" style but swapped its default blue palette for coffee browns and creams. The chart colours are blue for Online and caramel for Cafés, which colour-blind users can still tell apart. The fonts are Fira Sans and Fira Code from Google Fonts. Icons are inline SVG, and there are no remote images.

**Additions you didn't ask for**
- **Search:** typing in the search field filters the recent orders, products and café tables, and pressing `/` jumps to it.
- **In-page links:** the navigation items scroll to the matching section on this page, since the other pages don't exist. Customers has no section of its own, so it jumps to the KPI cards.
- **Motion:** animations are turned off for users who have reduced motion set on their device.
